correctionNotes: W-shaped tuning: elevated sub/mid-bass (+7-8 dB at 20-100 Hz), forward upper mids (~+14 dB pinna gain at 2.5 kHz), and a secondary treble peak (~+12 dB at 10 kHz).
Mid-bass emphasis (100-200 Hz) is the defining character; trim modestly toward the IEF target but preserve some warmth to keep the musical intent.
The 5-5.5 kHz presence peak can read as forward or slightly hard on vocals; a gentle cut here smooths the transition between upper mids and treble.
The 9-10 kHz treble peak adds sparkle and air but may cause sibilance on bright recordings; a moderate cut tames this without killing the extension.
The 7 kHz dip is a typical IEM coupler feature; do not chase it with EQ.
Lower mids (300-600 Hz) are slightly pulled back relative to the bass and upper mids; a small lift can restore vocal body if needed.
signature: W-shaped single-DD tuning: well-extended, punchy bass with mid-bass emphasis; forward, emotional upper mids and vocals; smooth treble with extra sparkle near 10 kHz. Described as a 'neutral+' everyday IEM with natural coherence and musicality.
source: Bloom Audio squig.link measurement (IEC 711 clone), July 2026. Corroborated by Bloom Audio written review, Head-Fi review (Pseudonym031), and eddie0817 WordPress impressions.
